subject: EdgeLabs commercial stitch: pricing reconciliation & packaging options
messages:
From: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@edgelabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Sood <priya.sood@edgelabs.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — edge replacement commercial data and packaging questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we're evaluating a potential move off our current inference vendor and want to understand how Redwood would map to our existing spend and entitlements. High level asks:

- Can you show a side-by-side of equivalent capacity (50M tokens/month, 6 concurrent long-running sessions, KV-prefetch behavior) for the models we use?
- We need a clear recommendation for credits vs discount structure for a 12-month committed plan.
- Any one-time migration credits or onboarding assistance you can provide (engineering hours, playbook) — we have significant KV cache warmup and prefix caching to port.

I attached a usage export (edgelabs_usage_Q2_2026.xlsx) and a short doc with replacement requirements. If you can return a consolidated worksheet with one recommended commercial path plus a backup lower-commit option, that would be ideal.

Timeline: procurement is targeting a commercial decision by Aug 6.

Best,
Taylor Chen
Senior PM, Platform
EdgeLabs

Attachments: edgelabs_usage_Q2_2026.xlsx, edge_replacement_requirements.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@edgelabs.com>
Cc: Priya Sood <priya.sood@edgelabs.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — edge replacement commercial data and packaging questions

Hi Taylor — thanks for the sheet and for laying out the timeline.

I reviewed the usage export quickly and looped in Jordan (sales lead for EdgeLabs) to align on commercial levers. A few quick clarifying questions before we build the workbook:

- The 6 concurrent long sessions — are they steady (24/7) or bursty during business hours? That changes the Dedicated sizing vs burst capacity.
- For model fidelity: do you need 8k context variants only, or are there any 32k sequences in the feed?
- Any contractual dealbreakers (data residency, SOC 2 artifact timing) we should bake into the proposal?

Assuming steady concurrency and mostly 8k context, our typical offers are:
1) Reserved commit (12 months): X% discount on hosted unit price + migration credits (one-time) tied to a commit bucket.
2) Hybrid: smaller commit with dedicated reserved pools for the hot paths and hosted fallback for spikes.

I'll produce a three-line commercial workbook (parity replacement, conservative commit, and hybrid) with the numeric math and recommended play. Expect the doc by Mon EOD (Jul 26).

Quick ask: can you confirm whether the current vendor is offering any counter-concession (credits/onboarding) so we can match appropriately?

Thanks — Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sood <priya.sood@edgelabs.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:22:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — edge replacement commercial data and packaging questions

Karthik / Jordan — quick answers to your clarifying questions:

- Concurrency: the 6 long-running sessions are steady for core inference (nightly batch + business hours), but we also see a ~2x spike for 3 hours/day. So steady with a short daily peak.
- Context: mostly 8k; we have a handful (~5% of tokens) for 30k sequences tied to research workloads. Those can be routed differently if needed.
- Contractual: SOC 2 Type II required within 60 days of go-live; data residency remains US only. Procurement will want a short statement of evidence for SOC 2 timing.

EdgeLabs is currently on a competitor plan that committed to a 15% migration credit over three months and a dedicated onboarding SRE engagement (20 hours) for warmup.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Procurement, EdgeLabs

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@edgelabs.com>, Priya Sood <priya.sood@edgelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 09:00:13 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft concession workbook + ask for pricing inputs

Jordan / Marcus — I drafted the attached concession workbook (redwood_concession_workbook.xlsx) with three scenarios: parity replacement, conservative 12m commit, and hybrid reserved+hosted. Highlights:

- Parity replacement: match economic footprint (token units + 6 concurrent slots) and offer a 12% migration credit applied as monthly bill credits over first 3 months. We hedge with a 6-week SLA ramp clause rather than a full 30-day SLA from day 1.
- Conservative commit (12m): 20% unit discount for a $120k/month commit (equivalent runtime capacity) + 40 hours onboarding SRE hours (booked as time & materials up to $22k) and a 6-week warmup playbook.
- Hybrid: smaller $60k/month commit with dedicated pool for the 6 steady sessions, hosted fallback for spikes, 15% migration credit, and 20 hours SRE.

Questions for pricing: what is the unit price per 1k tokens we should use for the workbook (hosted baseline), and can we justify a 20% discount at the $120k/month commit level with a staged ROI write-up? Also confirm whether we can commit to SOC 2 evidence within 45 days as part of the offer (EdgeLabs asked for 60).

I'll reply back to Taylor/Priya with the worksheet and a commercial recommendation once you confirm pricing inputs.

Thanks,
Karthik

(Attachment: redwood_concession_workbook.xlsx)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@edgelabs.com>, Priya Sood <priya.sood@edgelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: draft concession workbook + ask for pricing inputs

Team / EdgeLabs — thanks for the patience. Marcus and I worked through the numbers and here's the offer we'd like to present:

Commercial recommendation (single consolidated path with fallback):

1) Primary: 12-month commit at $125,000/month (estimated equivalent to current footprint + headroom).
   - Unit discount: 18% off hosted list unit price.
   - Migration support: $25,000 one-time credit applied across first invoice and 30 hours of onboarding SRE at no charge (covers warmup + prefix/KV cache migration).
   - SLA & ramp: Standard SLA with a 6-week measured ramp; full SLA credits kick in after successful warmup.

2) Fallback: 6-month trial hybrid (no long-term commit) with dedicated pool for steady sessions and hosted fallback for spikes. 15% migration credit.

Additional concessions:
- SOC 2 evidence: yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II artifacts within 45 days post-signature and a named compliance contact.
- No-equals clause: we will include a 90-day exit window with prorated credits if performance regressions are documented.

Next steps: if EdgeLabs is comfortable, we'll produce a short term sheet + DocuSign package and a technical handoff workbook. Taylor/Priya — can you confirm the procurement approver list so we populate the contract signers? Our goal is to get to signature by Aug 10 to meet your Aug 6 internal window with an expedited review.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeLabs commercial stitch: pricing reconciliation & packaging options

Jordan / Karthik — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. Procurement and platform have reviewed the proposed numbers. A couple of asks before we go to signature:

1) Can you reframe the $25k migration credit as a 3-month bill credit schedule (so it offsets the initial invoices) and include a line-item that 30 SRE hours are committed and booked against the onboarding credit?
2) We would like the 90-day exit window to be symmetric (both parties) and limited to documented performance regressions or force majeure (we'll have legal redline language).
3) Please include an explicit callout that the hybrid fallback will preserve token parity (no hidden unit conversions) during the 6-month pilot.

If you can send a one-page term sheet with those edits, procurement can route for approval immediately. We're aiming to get signers locked in by Wed Aug 4.

Best,
Taylor Chen
Senior PM, Platform
EdgeLabs

Attachments referenced: none (we reviewed the workbook)
